blocks.content: Certain acts shall not constitute an infringement of copyright, including fair dealing with any work for private or personal use.

rows: No prior consent needed from copyright holder
Education, research, criticism, and news reporting
Protected from civil and criminal liability
Attracts civil remedies and criminal penalties

items: Section 52 of the Copyright Act, 1957 is frequently tested regarding statutory exceptions and fair dealing principles.
Distinguish clearly between fair dealing for personal research and unauthorized commercial reproduction.
Note that judicial proceedings and reporting of parliamentary proceedings are completely exempted from copyright claims.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Section 52 of the Copyright Act, 1957 specifies acts that do not constitute an infringement of copyright.
Fair dealing with any work for private or personal use, including research, criticism, or review, is legally protected.
Educational exemptions permit reproduction of works by teachers or pupils during the course of instruction.
Reporting of current events and current affairs in print or broadcast media is exempted from copyright liability.
